summary: Brass: Birmingham is a tight, punishing economic engine-builder where every action is a resource trade-off and the board state constantly threatens to lock you out of profitable moves. Two eras force you to build, network, and sell in overlapping cycles, with the greatest tension coming from timing your own development against the flip-and-sell demand of rivals.
praised: Extremely tight, elegant economic engine with almost no wasted design space
Deep, multi-layered strategy with a very high skill ceiling
Strong tension between short-term efficiency and long-term positioning
Beautiful, functional production and tactile components
High replayability due to variable player powers and market fluctuations
criticised: Steep learning curve and heavy rules overhead for new players
Can feel punishing or swingy for first-timers who misjudge the link/build economy
Downtime between turns in higher player counts
Some find the theme thin dressing over a pure optimization puzzle

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via network/market competition

scoring.why: Victory points accumulate from canal/rail links and flipped industry tiles across two scoring rounds, rewarding efficient chains of development, building, and selling rather than any single dominant strategy
